title: Neural mechanisms of mindfulness: reduced neural reactivity to social-evaluative threat accounts for mindfulness intervention effects on inflammatory gene expression
authors: Blades RB, Boyle CC, Eisenberger NI, Cole SW, Korecki JRT, Fuligni AJ, Bower JE.
design: Randomized controlled trial; registered single-blind (outcome assessors)
summary: After six weeks, the meditation group showed lower neural responses to social-evaluative threat and lower inferred NF-κB activity. The gene-regulation difference lost statistical significance after adjustment for the neural-response change.
limitation: A small waitlist-controlled trial. Promoter analysis estimates transcription-factor activity; the analysis does not establish a causal neural mechanism.

design: Secondary imaging and transcriptomic analysis of a randomized trial

title: The Moderating Role of Genetics on the Effectiveness of the Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction for Breast Cancer (MBSR(BC)) Program on Cognitive Impairment.

summary: In 128 breast-cancer survivors randomised to MBSR or education/support, variants including DRD2 rs6277 were associated with differences in cognitive response to the intervention.
limitation: This was a small exploratory moderator analysis across multiple variants. It measured genotype, not altered gene expression, and is not a validated genetic predictor of treatment response.

title: Effect of a Web-Based Heartfulness Program on the Mental Well-Being, Biomarkers, and Gene Expression Profile of Health Care Students: Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Thimmapuram J, Patel KD, Bhatt D, Chauhan A, Madhusudhan D, Bhatt KK, Deshpande S, Budhbhatti U, Joshi C.
design: Randomized controlled trial; blinding not reported
summary: At 12 weeks, RNA sequencing identified 292 upregulated and 1,180 downregulated genes in the meditation group relative to controls. Reported stress and distress improved. IL-6 protein fell in both groups, with a larger reduction in controls.
limitation: An exploratory trial with an inactive comparator and exclusion of participants missing follow-up. Enrichment analysis does not establish changes in every gene belonging to a pathway.

title: Longitudinal DNA methylation in parent-infant pairs impacted by intergenerational social adversity: An RCT of the Michigan Model of Infant Mental Health Home Visiting
authors: Petroff RL, Jester J, Riggs J, Alfafara E, Springer K, Kerr N, Issa M, Hall A, Rosenblum K, Goodrich JM, Muzik M, Michigan Collaborative for Infant Mental Health Research.
summary: Infant BDNF methylation showed a possible decrease after the home-visiting psychotherapy programme. Most maternal molecular associations and intervention effects were absent.
limitation: The intervention includes multiple relational components. The results do not isolate particular spoken words, and the molecular findings were mixed.

title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Reduces Proinflammatory Gene Regulation But Not Systemic Inflammation Among Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Lindsay EK, Marsland AL, Cole SW, Dutcher JM, Greco CM, Wright AGC, Brown KW, Creswell JD.
summary: MBSR reduced inferred NF-κB activity relative to the active comparison programme (d=0.17; p=0.028). It did not reduce circulating IL-6 or C-reactive protein. CREB, IRF and glucocorticoid-receptor pathway differences were not statistically significant.
limitation: The gene-regulation signal was small and did not translate into a measured reduction in systemic inflammation. Pathway activity was inferred from RNA profiles.

title: Predicting psychosocial intervention response from baseline gene expression
authors: Ricon-Becker I, West TN, Fredrickson BL, Kaplan DM, Mehl MR, Raison CL, Cole SW.
design: Prediction analyses across two randomized trials

authors: Graham B, Jin Y, Bazeley P, Husni E, Calabrese LH.

title: Mindfulness meditation for younger breast cancer survivors: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Bower JE, Crosswell AD, Stanton AL, Crespi CM, Winston D, Arevalo J, Ma J, Cole SW, Ganz PA.
design: Randomized controlled trial; blinding not reported
quotes: ["“A brief, mindfulness‐based intervention demonstrated preliminary short‐term efficacy in reducing stress, behavioral symptoms, and proinflammatory signaling in younger breast cancer survivors”","“women in the mindfulness group who practiced more frequently did evidence lower levels of IL‐6 at the post‐treatment assessment”","“our trial indicates that the benefits of mindfulness may extend to genomic markers of inflammation, including reductions in proinflammatory gene expression and activity of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF‐ κ B”"]
summary: Meditation reduced perceived stress and proinflammatory gene expression after treatment. Depression improvement was not statistically significant. Most psychological and behavioural benefits were not maintained at three months.
limitation: A preliminary waitlist-controlled trial in a specific survivor population. Molecular changes do not establish a reduction in cancer recurrence or progression.

title: Community singing intervention reduces maternal salivary cytokines and enhances maternal-infant cortisol synchrony in postnatal depression: biological findings from the SHAPER-PND trial
authors: Kirkpatrick M, Priestley K, Bind RH, Rebecchini L, Borsini A, Estevao C, Hazelgrove K, Laijawala R, Alford S, Woods AJ, Crane N, Manoharan M, Burton A, Dye H, Osborn T, Greenwood L, Dazzan P, Fancourt D, Pariante C.
design: Biomarker analysis within a randomized trial
summary: After the first community-singing session, salivary IL-6 decreased by 26% in the singing group. The time-by-group interaction for IL-6 was significant. Later analyses also examined mother–infant cortisol synchrony and communication.
limitation: This measured salivary cytokine protein, not IL6 transcription. The biological subset was unbalanced, and speech correlations do not isolate the causal effect of particular words.

authors: Chen D, Gomzyakova E, Gu Y, Zhang Y, Hofmann SG, Liu X.

authors: Goldstein L, Romagnoli D, Nidich S.

summary: In 1,458 employees, an eight-week digital meditation programme improved perceived stress relative to waitlist, with an effect size of 0.85 at eight weeks and 0.71 at four months.
limitation: Participants volunteered, most were women, and the comparator did not match attention. Greater use correlated with improvement but was not itself randomised.

summary: A 26-person internet mantram pilot in breast-cancer survivors established delivery feasibility and reported exploratory changes in stress, spiritual wellbeing and selected serum cytokines.

title: Health Care Workers' Need for Headspace: Findings From a Multisite Definitive Randomized Controlled Trial of an Unguided Digital Mindfulness-Based Self-help App to Reduce Healthcare Worker Stress.
authors: Taylor H, Cavanagh K, Field AP, Strauss C.
summary: In 2,182 NHS staff, a digital mindfulness app produced a small but statistically significant reduction in stress relative to an active digital control over 4.5 months, with additional benefits on several wellbeing measures.
limitation: Effects were small and burnout and sickness absence did not improve significantly. Engagement was limited; this supports a scalable adjunct rather than a substitute for organisational support.

title: Effect of meditation on psychological distress and brain functioning: A randomized controlled study.
authors: Travis F, Valosek L, Konrad A, Link J, Salerno J, Scheller R, Nidich S.
summary: In 96 school-district staff, Transcendental Meditation improved mood and distress relative to waitlist over four months. An EEG subset of 79 participants also showed changes in the study's Brain Integration Scale.
limitation: The EEG composite is a study-specific measure, not proof of globally improved brain function. A waitlist does not isolate practice-specific effects from support and expectancy.

title: Effect of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction vs Cognitive Behavioral Therapy or Usual Care on Back Pain and Functional Limitations in Adults With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Cherkin DC, Sherman KJ, Balderson BH, Cook AJ, Anderson ML, Hawkes RJ, Hansen KE, Turner JA.
summary: At 26 weeks, meaningful functional improvement occurred in 60.5% receiving MBSR, 57.7% receiving CBT and 44.1% receiving usual care. Both active treatments improved pain outcomes; no significant difference separated MBSR and CBT.
limitation: These are clinical pain and function outcomes, not molecular measurements. The trial does not establish superiority over CBT.

authors: Bormann JE, Oman D, Walter KH, Johnson BD.

authors: Bowen S, Witkiewitz K, Clifasefi SL, Grow J, Chawla N, Hsu SH, Carroll HA, Harrop E, Collins SE, Lustyk MK, Larimer ME.
summary: In 286 adults completing substance-use treatment, mindfulness-based relapse prevention reduced substance-use days and heavy drinking at 12 months relative to standard relapse prevention and usual aftercare.
